sounds.intro: Portuguese swallows many unstressed vowels, so it sounds quicker than it looks. Learn these sounds first.
rows: eh when stressed; a short "uh" or silent when unstressed
oh when stressed; "oo" at the end of a word
nasal vowels: air goes through the nose, no n sound
nasal "ow", like "ow" in "now" through the nose

phrases.title: Formal and informal
phrases.note: tu (informal): friends, family, young people. o senhor / a senhora (formal): strangers, older people, work. With the formal "you", the verb is in the he / she form. Você is common but can feel cool in Portugal. Use o senhor or a senhora when unsure.

grammar.title: Pronouns
text: The pronoun is often dropped, because the verb ending shows who is speaking. For formal "you", use o senhor / a senhora.

grammar.title: Singular and plural
text: Most plurals add -s: casa → casas. Words ending in a consonant add -es. Words in -ão change: pão → pães, mão → mãos, limão → limões. Words in -l change: animal → animais. Articles change: o → os, a → as, um → uns, uma → umas.

grammar.title: Ser: to be (who or what)
text: Ser: identity, origin, jobs, descriptions, time.

grammar.title: Ter: to have
text: Ter is also used for age and feelings: tenho dezasseis anos, tenho fome, tenho sede.

grammar.title: Regular verbs (present tense)
text: Three families: -ar, -er, -ir. Drop the ending, add the new one. Falar (to speak):

grammar.title: Ir: to go
text: Going to do something soon: ir + infinitive. Vou comer = I am going to eat.

grammar.title: Basic sentences
text: Order: subject, verb, rest. The adjective usually comes after the noun and agrees with it. You can drop the pronoun.
rows: add time or place at the end
ex: we live in a big house

grammar.title: Negation
text: Put não before the verb. Double negatives are normal: não tenho nada.
Put não before the verb: eu não falo. Double negatives are normal: não tenho nada (I do not have anything). nada = nothing, ninguém = nobody, nunca = never.
ex: I do not have a car
he does not work on Sundays

grammar.title: Asking questions
text: Yes or no question: same words as a statement, with a rising voice. Or add "não é?" (isn't it?).

grammar.title: Formal vs informal
text: tu / teu for friends and family. o senhor / a senhora, with the he / she verb form, for strangers and work.

grammar.title: Past and future (simple)
text: Past (simple): -ei, -aste, -ou, -ámos, -aram for -ar verbs. Future: ir + infinitive, or infinitive + -ei, -ás, -á, -emos, -ão.

grammar.title: Commands
text: Informal (tu): -ar verbs use the ele form (fala), -er / -ir verbs too (come, escreve). Negative: não + the -es / -as form (não fales). Formal (o senhor): fale, coma.

grammar.title: Can, must, want
text: poder (can), dever / ter de (must), querer (want) + infinitive: posso nadar, tenho de ir, quero comer. Não deves = you must not.
ex: I do not want to eat

grammar.title: In, on, at
text: em = in / on / at; sobre / em cima de = on; debaixo de = under; ao lado de = next to; perto de = near; às nove = at nine.
ex: the book is on the table
o livro está em cima da mesa
oo LEE-vroo shTAH ehm SEE-mah dah MEH-zah
the cat is under the table
o gato está debaixo da mesa
oo GAH-too shTAH deh-BAH-ee-shoo dah MEH-zah
the shop is next to the bank
a loja fica ao lado do banco
ah LOH-zhah FEE-kah ow LAH-doo doo BAHN-koo
the park is near the station
o parque fica perto da estação
oo PAR-k FEE-kah PEHR-too dah shtah-SOWN
the key is in the bag

grammar.title: Comparing things
text: mais + adjective + (do) que = more than (mais alto do que eu). menos... que = less than. o mais... = the most. melhor = better, pior = worse.
ex: pequeno, mais pequeno, o mais pequeno
peh-KEH-noo mighsh peh-KEH-noo oo mighsh peh-KEH-noo
isto é melhor do que aquilo
EESH-too eh meh-LYOR doo k ah-KEE-loo
isto é pior do que aquilo
EESH-too eh pee-OR doo k ah-KEE-loo
ela é mais alta do que eu
EH-lah eh mighsh AHL-tah doo k EH-oo
Tashkent é maior do que Samarcanda
tahsh-KEHNT eh mah-ee-OR doo k sah-mar-KAHN-dah
